summary: The recorded base already contained a reusable flydsl.extension.coop BlockScan with explicit inclusive and exclusive forms, scalar and per-thread Vector inputs, optional initialization, and block aggregate variants. Its existing focused GPU suite passed before changes. This contribution adds an independent multi-block numerical regression that pins wave-boundary outputs and documents the public contract and current limitations; it does not claim the broader common-building-block proposal is complete.

tests.what_was_measured: The checked-out implementation's 62 existing block-scan tests passed on the assigned GPU before this contribution. Coverage included inclusive/exclusive scans, integer and float types, scalar and Vector inputs, block aggregates, initialization, 1-1024 power-of-two thread counts, multidimensional blocks, and universal/dispatched paths.

64 GPU tests passed after adding inclusive and exclusive multi-block regressions. The new reference uses host torch.cumsum independently per block and explicitly checks lanes 0, 63, 64, and 127 on gfx950. Raw output: reports/j-6e7fec7ab628/raw/test_block_scan.txt
All 326 cooperative extension tests passed, covering the block-scan change alongside warp scans and block reductions. Raw output: reports/j-6e7fec7ab628/raw/test_coop.txt

The real GPU stream-compaction example passed by comparing scan-derived output positions and values with an independent CPU boolean-filter reference. Raw output: reports/j-6e7fec7ab628/raw/block_scan_example.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the numerical tests and example with torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4. Device evidence: reports/j-6e7fec7ab628/raw/gpu_environment.txt
remaining_limitations: The base already contained the BlockScan implementation, so no failing implementation defect was found; this PR strengthens independent boundary coverage and public documentation rather than duplicating the implementation.
BlockScan currently requires a power-of-two number of threads and all threads in the specialized block to participate together.
Only the WARP_SCANS block policy is implemented; RAKING and RAKING_MEMOIZE remain explicitly unimplemented.
The public operation set is limited to associative ReductionOp ADD, MUL, MIN, and MAX rather than arbitrary callables.
Validation was performed only on the assigned gfx950 GPU; other AMD architectures remain unverified in this job.
No native C++ source changed, so the prepared native rebuild was not applicable and was not run.
The optional Python style checker could not run because black and ruff are absent from the prepared interpreter; git diff --check passed and the focused/full GPU tests passed.
